name: Why is a kitchen backsplash necessary instead of just painted drywall?

mainEntity.name: Why is a kitchen backsplash necessary instead of just painted drywall?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen backsplash protects drywall from moisture and grease, makes cleaning easier, and significantly enhances visual appeal. Bare or painted drywall behind sinks and stoves absorbs grease, water splatters, and food stains, which can lead to staining, drywall softening, or mold growth over time. Wiping painted drywall repeatedly can wear away the finish and leave dull spots. A tiled backsplash creates an impermeable barrier that wipes clean with mild soap and water, shielding the wall structure while tying together your countertops, cabinets, and appliances into a cohesive design.
acceptedAnswer.description: A backsplash shields drywall from water, grease, and food stains while creating a durable, easy-to-clean surface that protects your walls and unifies kitchen finishes.
